Jagdish Chandra Purohit .............Petitioner
Vs.
Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali Uttarakhand University & others
...........Respondents
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.
Hon'ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Piyush Garg and Mr. Shakti Saurabh Purohit, learned
counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for respondent nos.1
and 2.
3. Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr.
C.S. Dalakoti, learned counsel for respondent no.3.
4. The post of Assistant Professor (Statistics) was advertised
showing it to be reserved for Economically Weaker Sections
category (EWS category). The petitioner is EWS category
candidate and after short-listing, he participated in the interview
along with respondent no.3, who, admittedly, does not belong to
EWS category. However, respondent no.3 was recommended for
appointment against the vacancy in question.
5. In the counter-affidavit filed by the University, it is
admitted that respondent no.3 does not belong to EWS category
and it is stated that consequently, he has not been given
appointment.
6. Respondent no.3 has filed a counter-affidavit and has
placed reliance on Section 3(3) of the Uttarakhand Public
Services (Reservation for Economically Weaker Sections) Act,
2019, which is as follows:-
"3(3) If, in any recruitment year any vacancy reserved for
Economically Weaker Section cannot be filled up due to non-availability of a suitable candidate, then such vacancies for that
particular recruitment year shall not be carried forward to the next
recruitment year as backlog and such vacancy shall be filled up

from a suitable candidate belonging to General category."
7. As per own case of respondent no.3, he could be
recommended for appointment against the vacancy reserved for
EWS category only if the petitioner had been adjudged as non-suitable for the post in question.
8. In the counter-affidavit filed by the University, it has not
disclosed the criteria prescribed for adjudging the suitability of
the candidate during interview, nor has brought on record the
marks obtained by the petitioner. It is stated that the marks
obtained by candidates have been kept in a sealed cover and, in
case, this Court would direct, the same shall be produced before
it. Respondent no.3 has obtained 21 marks out 25 in the
interview. However, marks of the petitioner are not on record.
9. In order to resolve the controversy, the University is
required to disclose the criteria, if any, prescribed by it for
adjudging suitability of candidates during interview and also
place on record the marks obtained by the petitioner in the
interview to enable the Court to examine whether the petitioner
was entitled for appointment against the post in question, or not.
10. List after two weeks.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
